headline_draft: Claude Code v2.1.234 ships GitLab MR support, session continuation, and cross-session collaboration via @ mentions
summary: Anthropic released Claude Code 2.1.234 on August 17, 2026, adding GitLab merge-request support in the worktree view, automatic session continuation when usage limits reset, and @ mention syntax to reference other Claude Code sessions for multi-session collaboration. The update also includes stronger credential-leak protections and memory limits to prevent runaway build commands. These changes lower friction in multi-developer workflows and make long-running, stateful work across sessions more tractable for teams using Claude Code as their primary development environment.
why_pm: As PMs build more with AI agents and Claude Code, understanding the developer experience directly informs product strategy decisions—credential safety, session management, and cross-session workflow are now table-stakes for tools targeting serious development work.
key_facts: Adds GitLab merge-request support in worktree view
Session auto-continuation when usage limits reset
Memory limits on build commands to prevent freeze-ups
quotes: Claude Code 2.1.234 now automatically continues your session when usage limits reset and includes stronger security protections against credential leaks.

headline_draft: Consensus: PMs must become 'AI-literate builders' — judgment and clear specs are now the scarcest skill
summary: Multiple sources from August 2026 converge on a single message: the PM role has fundamentally shifted from feature delivery to systems thinking and judgment under AI acceleration. Andrew Ng frames it bluntly: 'As coding becomes cheaper, teams will need more product management work as a fraction of the total workforce. Given a clear specification for what to build, AI is making the building itself much faster and cheaper. This will significantly increase demand for people who can come up with clear specs for valuable things to build.' Astasia Myers adds: 'AI makes code cheap, but product learning isn't. The real bottleneck is knowing what to build next.' PMs who operate with pre-AI mental models—feature lists, consensus-driven roadmaps, spec by committee—are increasingly out of step with how AI-native teams execute.
why_pm: If you're evaluating your PM toolkit and mindset, this is the forcing function. You can no longer compete on execution velocity (AI handles that). Your value is in judgment: what to build, why, for whom, and how to measure it. Spending time on POV development, customer signal synthesis, and hypothesis clarity will pay more than Jira mastery.
